title: Productivity, workspaces, and AI-native browsers

evidenceConventions.documentaryFacts: Availability, versions, restrictions and lifecycle are statements in retrieved documents, not installed-browser observations.
evidenceConventions.documentedBehavior: Vendor-documented features describe the maker's procedures or offering; they have not been exercised by this project.
evidenceConventions.vendorClaims: Performance, privacy, security effectiveness, integration counts and productivity claims remain attributed assertions.
evidenceConventions.recommendations: Recommendation candidates are Chrome design hypotheses pending baseline and feasibility assessment, not endorsements of the source products.
evidenceConventions.dates: Publication dates are null when not established. Specific article metadata dates retain their provenance. Effective dates, release-entry dates, relative updates and conflicting date indications are recorded separately.
evidenceConventions.lifecycle: Product lifecycle is distinct from feature maturity, channel, platform and subscription availability. Historical or experimental evidence is not an active-product recommendation.

conversion.origin: Completed R04 research report: Productivity, workspaces, and AI-native browsers
notes: The conversion preserves the report's 11 product cards, 62 substantive feature entries, 65 cited URLs and 10 proposal candidates.
Combined entries remain combined so that the feature count maps one-to-one to the original numbered research entries.
Short quotations are drawn from previously retrieved public source bodies. Raw retrieval transcripts and private operating context are excluded.
Some source dates were conservatively changed to null rather than treating a template date, effective date or disputed metadata value as publication.

recommendationCandidates.title: Identity-aware workspaces and link routing
recommendationCandidates.description: Investigate whether workspace organization can expose active identity and route links predictably, drawing on Zen/Floorp container defaults, Dia profile rules and Wavebox's explicit hierarchy.
acceptanceQuestions: Can a user open the same service under two accounts in one organized window and clearly see which identity is active?
Can external links be routed predictably without conflating visual tab groups, cookie containers and full profiles?
tradeoffs: Identity convenience versus understandable isolation boundaries and routing precedence.
limitations: No missing Chrome capability is established. Baseline must record browser version, operating system, account, region and rollout.
Floorp is temporarily stabilization-focused; source-browser examples are not installation recommendations.

recommendationCandidates.title: Durable, disposable, and completed tab states
recommendationCandidates.description: Investigate explicit saved-versus-temporary tab states and recoverable completion, using Arc resettable pins/archive, SigmaOS Done/locked pages and Dia nested organization as qualified precedents.
acceptanceQuestions: Can temporary work be closed or unloaded without deleting saved project structure?
Can users undo mistaken completion and restore a named project?
Does nesting provide value beyond Chrome's existing group model for representative workflows?
tradeoffs: Explicit state labels and recoverability versus surprising automatic deletion and added hierarchy.
limitations: Arc is sunset-announced and its features are historical; SigmaOS maintenance remains unknown. Neither is recommended as an active replacement.
The candidate is a Chrome design question, not a demonstrated defect or missing feature.

recommendationCandidates.title: Saved multitasking layouts with preview promotion
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare preview-to-tab/split transitions and reusable layouts using Zen Glance, Floorp subdivisions/panels and Dia remembered splits.
acceptanceQuestions: Can a transient link preview become a tab or split without losing context?
Can a two-to-four-pane project layout be saved and restored?
Are keyboard focus order, minimum pane sizes and narrow-screen behavior understandable?
tradeoffs: More simultaneous context versus small panes, resource cost and complex focus management.
limitations: Floorp's four-pane statement is version-qualified; Dia's remembered layout is homepage documentation, not tested restoration.
Chrome split-view, preview and extension equivalents remain unassessed.

recommendationCandidates.title: Discoverable command menu with intentional AI routing
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare named browser actions and explicit search-versus-AI routing using Arc/SigmaOS/Zen command surfaces and Shift's Tab-for-AI interaction.
acceptanceQuestions: Can users discover organization actions by name and inspect shortcut conflicts?
Can users explicitly choose AI versus ordinary search without involuntary routing?
Do deterministic browser commands remain usable without AI latency or a subscription?
tradeoffs: A unified entry point versus modal/keybinding conflicts and ambiguous intent routing.
limitations: Arc is a historical sunset precedent; SigmaOS support is unresolved. These are not active-browser endorsements.
Zen pre-release channels and historical entries require version-specific qualification; no Chrome gap is yet established.

recommendationCandidates.title: Per-workspace app dock and account-aware notifications
recommendationCandidates.description: Investigate account-labeled app presence, notifications and link rules based on Wavebox, Shift and historical Sidekick workflows.
acceptanceQuestions: Can two accounts of one service remain visible with unambiguous labels/badges and scoped notifications?
Do opened links consistently reach the intended account?
Which benefits require native browser integration rather than an app-catalog wrapper or an extension?
tradeoffs: Persistent app convenience versus notification overload, integration maintenance and account-boundary complexity.
limitations: Sidekick is discontinued and distributor-documented; it is historical inspiration, not an actively recommended solution.
Service, subscription and platform parity remain untested; Chrome and web-app equivalents need baseline comparison.

recommendationCandidates.title: Visible AI context and authority controls
recommendationCandidates.description: Investigate inspectable context and separate read/action permissions, using Shift context chips, historical Atlas site visibility/ephemeral identity, Comet policy controls and Neon's task scope.
acceptanceQuestions: Before execution, can users inspect selected tabs, history and connectors and choose Read Only versus Act?
Can users block sites or choose an ephemeral identity?
Does a global off control have unambiguous semantics, with policy precedence visible rather than silently overridden by domain exceptions?
tradeoffs: Convenient contextual automation versus understandable permission scope, identity separation and explicit controls.
limitations: Atlas is retired; its formerly preview controls are historical evidence only. Neon task/security descriptions have Early Access history and unverified stable maturity.
Comet's documented domain-rule precedence is not a locally reproduced bypass or a Chrome vulnerability.
No enforcement or data-flow test was performed; source examples are not security guarantees.

recommendationCandidates.title: Task-control view for concurrent browser agents
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare visible scope/status, queued steering and confirmation handling using Dia chat controls, Comet Background Assistants and Neon planned-step views.
acceptanceQuestions: Can users see task scope and status, pause/stop/take over, and edit queued requests?
Are foreground and background work clearly distinguished by platform?
Does the interface explain what Stop cancels, what has already committed and where completed outputs remain inspectable?
tradeoffs: Concurrent work versus state conflicts, confusing completion and incomplete cancellation.
limitations: Comet Max access is dated entitlement evidence; Android foreground limits differ. Dia AI pricing is incomplete, and Neon agents are subscription-limited.
Neon Early Access history is not promoted into a production-ready agent recommendation.
No concurrent task or stop behavior was reproduced; Chrome parity is unassessed.

recommendationCandidates.title: Inspectable reusable prompt recipes
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare Comet Shortcuts, Dia Skills and Neon Cards as reusable, inspectable instruction bundles while keeping recipe composition separate from action authority.
acceptanceQuestions: Can a recipe show the expanded prompt, selected sources, model and requested authority before submission?
Does importing or sharing a recipe avoid granting action permission?
Is there an explicit submission boundary after recipe composition?
tradeoffs: Repeatability and sharing versus opaque prompts, stale integrations and accidental authority transfer.
limitations: An announced shortcut library is not assumed shipped. Dia integrations have separate GA/beta stages and Neon Cards have paid/early-access qualifications.
No recipe was executed or shared, and existing Chrome equivalents were not assessed.

recommendationCandidates.title: Portable project/session artifacts and retirement-resilient recovery
recommendationCandidates.description: Investigate inspectable exports and recovery independent of a vendor account or retired service, using Dia Markdown export, Zen structured continuity and Arc/Atlas lifecycle lessons.
acceptanceQuestions: Can named groups, URLs, pin destinations and layout metadata be exported/imported in an inspectable format?
Can organization be recovered after service or account retirement?
Is portable project structure clearly separated from live cookies, passwords and signed-in sessions?
tradeoffs: Rich portable state versus interoperability, versioning and unintended sensitive-data inclusion.
limitations: Arc is sunset-announced and Atlas is retired; they are lifecycle case studies, not recommended products.
Dia export and Zen backups do not by themselves prove lossless round trips or current stable cross-device recovery.
No personal data or profile was examined; Chrome portability gaps remain unassessed.

recommendationCandidates.title: Task-oriented resource and attention overview
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare resource explanations organized around user projects/apps, using Wavebox Navigator and Floorp panel-unloading controls.
acceptanceQuestions: Can users identify which project or app consumes memory and CPU?
Can an inactive work context be suspended without losing its layout?
Does the grouping and explanation add actionable value beyond Chrome's existing performance surfaces?
tradeoffs: Actionable grouped information versus metric overhead, attribution ambiguity and unnecessary dashboard complexity.
limitations: No resource measurements or state-preservation tests were performed.
Floorp's feature pause demonstrates a maintenance priority, not an independently measured cost model or abandonment.
The proposal remains conditional on a Chrome baseline assessment.

Model lineups and exact usage limits are volatile and were not verified as a compatibility promise.
Current free/paid access is better supported than universal paid-only FAQ wording, but complete feature maturity remains unassessed.
This is a conversion of completed documentary research, not a fresh search or a browser reproduction. No tested browser versions are asserted.

Page extractors omitted some dates, headings and bodies. Generic template dates and footer years were not converted into publication dates; relative dates and disputed metadata are retained as qualifications.

Experimental, retired, sunset-announced and uncertain-maintenance products are retained as qualified evidence, not promoted to actively recommended replacements.

Issues is intentionally empty: the lane supplies product evidence and recommendation hypotheses, not locally reproduced defects or upstream report submissions.

features.title: Spaces, folders, and named pinned tabs
features.description: Arc's legacy action reference organizes the sidebar around named Spaces and folders, with actions to focus a Space, pin a tab to a named folder, and rename a tab.
platforms: Desktop Arc; legacy command reference, OS parity unverified

quotations.text: Pins a tab to a specific Folder

limitations: Historical design evidence from an undated command list; Arc is sunset-announced, not an active replacement recommendation.
Mac/Windows feature parity and present behavior were not tested.

features.title: Persistent pin destinations
features.description: Reset an individual pinned tab or an entire Space to originally pinned URLs, or deliberately replace a pin with the current page. Saved destinations are distinct from temporary navigation state.
platforms: Desktop Arc; legacy command reference, OS parity unverified
limitations: Legacy documented behavior, not a tested persistence or recovery guarantee.
Arc's announced sunset limits this to design inspiration.

features.title: Unified command bar
features.description: Navigation, tab and Space organization, settings, extension access and browser operations are collected in one action surface. The reference includes named extension lookup and organization commands.
platforms: Desktop Arc; legacy command reference, OS parity unverified
limitations: Reference includes obsolete actions; Notes/Easels were not counted as current functionality.
Historical command design is not evidence that Chrome lacks named actions or equivalent shortcuts.

features.title: Split views and Little Arc
features.description: The command list documents adding, removing and expanding split views, with split removal distinct from closing the underlying tab. Little Arc provides a separate small-window entry for transient browsing.
platforms: Desktop Arc; legacy command reference, OS parity unverified
limitations: Little Arc and split controls were not validated across operating systems.
Both are retained as historical interaction precedents for a sunset-announced product.

features.title: Today/Archive and sidebar recovery
features.description: The Today section distinguishes disposable tabs from persistent organization. The archive revisits manually and automatically closed tabs, while Restore Data brings back older sidebar states.
platforms: Desktop Arc; legacy command reference, OS parity unverified
limitations: No archive retention, restore accuracy or post-retirement recovery test was performed.
Legacy documentation must not be treated as a current service-continuity guarantee.

features.title: Profiles and hierarchy
features.description: Profiles separate tabs, logins and AI context, with link-routing rules for incoming URLs. November 12 Mac and Windows entries describe tab groups nested up to eight levels and controls for opening links inside groups.
limitations: Profile isolation and rule enforcement were not tested; visual grouping is not automatically an identity boundary.
Routing is first explicitly described in the November 5 Mac entry; complete release-by-release Windows parity is not asserted.

features.title: Remembered split layouts
features.description: Dia advertises simultaneous meeting/document views and remembered split layouts that can be reused for recurring meetings or focused work.
limitations: Homepage description does not establish the first ship date, maximum pane count or restoration fidelity.
No saved-layout interaction was exercised.

features.title: Live Work and meeting context
features.description: Live Work brings GitHub/Notion work surfaces and PR previews into tab organization; Better Meetings assembles meeting pages and related context. Morning Brief gathers work context, with November 19 entries adding estimated items read and contributing tools.
limitations: Requires relevant connected services and permissions; connector rollout and AI entitlements differ.
The quality, completeness and accuracy of briefs or live previews were not measured.

features.title: Contextual AI and reusable Skills
features.description: Ask about the current page or explicitly mention tabs, and reuse custom Skills. The October 15 Windows release adds Skills matching the Mac experience. Connected applications have independent rollout stages.
limitations: Figma is marked GA on November 12; Ashby/Dropbox are marked beta on October 29. This is not a blanket GA claim for every integration.
Current paid AI quotas/prices were not established, and shared Skills may be hosted publicly if the user chooses to share them.
No prompt, connector or AI task was executed.

features.title: Queue and steer ongoing chat
features.description: Queue, edit, reorder or redirect messages during ongoing work. Mac notes distinguish steering without cancelling in-flight tools from Send now interruption; Windows October 29 notes document queued and steerable messages while preserving generated work.
limitations: Chat access is subject to AI availability and unverified quotas.
Cancellation, pause and committed-action semantics were not tested; wording in release notes is not proof that every side effect can be stopped or undone.

features.title: Organization portability and control
features.description: November 19 Mac and Windows entries document exporting tabs, profiles and groups to Markdown. Windows notes also describe inactive-tab archiving and customizable shortcuts; both platforms document natural-language tab-group operations.
limitations: Markdown export does not establish a complete round-trip importer, credential transfer or layout preservation.
Archiving thresholds and shortcut parity differ by documented entry; AI-driven organization has separate entitlement limits.

features.title: Workspace-default containers
features.description: Assign cookie/session containers to a workspace, customize its identity, and optionally route new container tabs to the workspace using that default container.
limitations: Container separation is narrower than a full profile boundary.
No account-isolation or automatic-routing test was run.

features.title: Glance previews
features.description: Preview a linked website above the current tab, then dismiss it, promote it to a new tab or turn it into a split. Trigger modifiers are configurable, with special behavior for external links in Essentials and pinned tabs.
limitations: No preview focus, form-state or keyboard-navigation test was performed.
Manual descriptions, rather than the less precise homepage summary, define the behavior here.

features.title: Split interaction shortcuts
features.description: Join tabs using modifier-click or drag interactions and separate them through explicit split/un-split commands, making the layout transition part of tab management.
limitations: Living release log includes several iterations of shortcuts and layout behavior; a precise first-ship date was not established.
No current-platform interaction test or pane-limit claim.

features.title: Command surface
features.description: Search tabs and folders, scope search to a Space, and invoke actions such as new Space, reset pinned tab, duplicate tab or reopen closed tab from the command surface.
limitations: Documented command additions are not a measured discoverability or performance improvement.
No keybinding-conflict test or exact per-command release date was established.

features.title: Live folders and link routing
features.description: Populate folders from GitHub issues, pull requests or RSS feeds, and use Space Routing to send incoming links into a selected work context.
limitations: Release notes record fixes for changing GitHub interfaces; integration reliability was not tested.
Source account access and routing precedence require separate runtime assessment.

features.title: Structure-aware continuity
features.description: Sync Spaces, folders and tabs through a Mozilla account, optionally including normal tabs; share structured collections and split views by link; use documented cross-platform local profile backups.
limitations: A Mozilla account and opt-in are required for the described sync; initial enablement merges local and cloud Spaces.
Earlier window sync was marked experimental. This conversion does not imply all sync features or old limitations are stable/resolved.
No backup, restore, sharing or conflict-resolution test was run.

features.title: Container-linked workspaces with archives
features.description: Assign a Firefox container to a workspace, archive its tab set and recover it from an archive view. Only one workspace is displayed per window; the documentation distinguishes shared workspace structures from individual tabs.
limitations: Behavior is documented as of 12.14.2; no archive or cross-window restoration test.
The browser is in a temporary stabilization period, and background-tab data preservation is not independently guaranteed.

features.title: Up to four simultaneous panes
features.description: Extend upstream Firefox split view with further subdivisions, arrangement controls and directional drag targets. The documented limit is four tabs at once as of Floorp 12.14.2.
limitations: The four-pane limit is version-qualified, not a claim about every future release.
No usability, focus-order, minimum-size or performance test.

features.title: Any-site web panels
features.description: Register websites in a persistent sidebar for one-click compact split views. Individual web panels can use a chosen container, width, zoom level and mobile/desktop user-agent setting.
limitations: A mobile user agent does not guarantee that a site changes layout.
Container enforcement, arbitrary-site compatibility and panel persistence were not tested.

features.title: Overlay/floating and unload controls
features.description: Use sidebar panels as overlays or movable/resizable floating views, open them on hover, keep them resident or unload them when hidden. Internal tools and supported extension pages can also be exposed as panels.
limitations: Some extensions cannot be displayed in the sidebar.
Unloading requires a later reload; form-state preservation and resource savings were not measured.

features.title: Integrated notes and desktop customization
features.description: Formatted notes and image attachments live in the Panel Sidebar and are documented to sync through Firefox Sync. The homepage also advertises web-app windows, UI customization and mouse gestures as desktop customization options.
limitations: Sync requires the relevant account setup; no cross-device synchronization or formatting test was run.
Homepage customization claims do not establish detailed per-platform web-app or gesture parity.

features.title: Tabs as tasks
features.description: Treat vertical pages as tasks: mark them Done when complete, lock pages that should remain available, and undo accidental closures.
limitations: Advertised/documented behavior does not establish current maintenance or successful onboarding.
Not an actively maintained-product recommendation; closure/undo was not tested.

features.title: Workspaces with optional separate cookies
features.description: Organize pages and web apps by project, optionally separate cookies to maintain multiple logins, create private workspaces and start from prefilled templates.
limitations: Current lifecycle is unresolved; no cookie-isolation or private-workspace test.
Homepage now advertises unlimited Basic workspaces, conflicting with the older FAQ's paid limit; no legacy limit is treated as current.

features.title: Lazy Search and command filtering
features.description: Space opens Lazy Search across pages, workspaces, tags and actions, while Cmd+K applies a commands-only filter. The same surface can jump to existing pages or create documents in supported tools.
limitations: Legacy documentation does not establish present integration availability or performance.
Current browser maintenance remains unresolved.

features.title: Single-key and split semantics
features.description: Use single keys for Done and Focus, and a consistent Shift modifier to open links/searches or complete a page in the second pane. Shortcut priority can be changed when browser commands conflict with web apps.
limitations: The tutorial specifies two pages, not arbitrary multi-pane tiling.
No keyboard-layout, accessibility or shortcut-conflict test; maintenance status is unresolved.

features.title: Quick Search and previews
features.description: A temporary Quick Search workspace returns to the prior work context after the page is completed. Command-hover previews the destination behind a link without fully opening it.
limitations: No preview-state or return-navigation test was run.
Still-advertised features are not proof of current maintenance.

features.title: Airis context interaction
features.description: Airis advertises Ask Anything, natural-language page finding, contextual explanations, multi-page Look it up research and interactive Simplify summaries.
limitations: Basic advertises limited Airis; homepage Pro/Max advertise greater usage at $20/$30 monthly, with currency and actual fulfillment unverified.
AI service operation, model availability, task quality and current maintenance remain unresolved.
Historical model mentions do not establish a current model catalog.

features.title: Persistent app sidebar and multiple app accounts
features.description: Historical distributor copy describes a persistent sidebar for web apps and extensions, multiple app accounts and custom web apps.
platforms: Historical desktop product; feature-specific OS matrix not recovered
limitations: Discontinued product; distributor marketing, not recovered maker documentation or a runtime test.
Does not establish continuity of app-account isolation in Comet.

features.title: Named sessions/workspaces
features.description: Historical Sessions/workspace copy describes grouping, saving, reopening and switching tab sets for personal, professional or project contexts.
platforms: Historical desktop product; feature-specific OS matrix not recovered
limitations: Unlimited sessions was a historical plan claim, not a current offer.
No saved-session fidelity, export or Comet migration test.

features.title: Unified search
features.description: Distributor-hosted product copy describes searching contacts, documents, mail and chats across work surfaces from one address bar.
platforms: Historical desktop product; feature-specific OS matrix not recovered
limitations: Search scope, indexing model, permissions and supported services were not independently verified.
Discontinued-product sales copy is design inspiration only.

features.title: Split view
features.description: Historical copy describes side-by-side documents, email and task lists in the browser's main screen.
platforms: Historical desktop product; feature-specific OS matrix not recovered
limitations: No pane count, layout persistence or platform parity established.
Retained as historical distributor evidence, not supported current functionality.

features.title: Focus tools
features.description: Historical productivity tools include muting notifications, redirecting distracting sites during work hours and keeping pinned tasks available across work surfaces.
platforms: Historical desktop product; feature-specific OS matrix not recovered
limitations: Scheduling, notification suppression and task persistence were not tested.
The discontinued product is not recommended as an active focus solution.

features.title: Explicit organization layers
features.description: Cookie-isolated Spaces contain Groups with individual tab strips and persistent Apps. Separate full Profiles have their own webdock and settings, making the hierarchy distinguish grouping from stronger isolation.

Actual isolation was not tested. Additional conceptual overhead is a hypothesis, not a measured usability result.

features.title: Multi-account app presence
features.description: Persistent app tabs expose unread badges, tooltips and custom notification sounds across multiple accounts. The Mini menu consolidates incoming work from webmail, messaging and collaboration tools.
limitations: App integrations are enhanced web tabs, not necessarily native applications or complete service integrations.
Notification accuracy, isolation and delivery were not tested; Basic plan limits apply.

features.title: Resizable splits and multiple windows
features.description: Split apps or tabs into resizable pages and use multiple windows, including simultaneous work in two accounts of the same service, such as separate calendars.
limitations: Maximum pane count, saved-layout restoration and edition entitlements were not established.
Vendor productivity language is not a measured time saving.

features.title: Brainbox and Chat with Settings
features.description: Brainbox offers contextual skills and selectable AI. Chat with Settings is a persistent setup conversation that can change browser settings and is available within Settings as well as chat history; it is described as free and outside Brainbox token allowances. The homepage says AI can be disabled.
limitations: The free settings-chat exception does not establish unlimited general Brainbox use or a current model catalog.
Settings mutation authority, confirmations, rollback and AI-disable enforcement were not tested.

features.title: Navigator resource overview
features.description: Navigator provides Spaces, List and Map views, with memory-sized Space tiles, CPU/memory sorting, extension resource usage and time/resource insights by work context and date range.
limitations: Documented in release 155.3.12; metric correctness, overhead and current plan entitlement were not measured.
No conclusion about superiority to Chrome's existing performance tools.

features.title: Work continuity and team templates
features.description: Synced Profiles and Wavebox Live distribute prepared app/group setups and updates to teams. Dashboards and persistent Smart Note checklists supplement the browser's work context.
limitations: Sync, Pro and team deployment have separate account/data/entitlement boundaries; exact paid rates were not recovered.
No template deployment, synchronization, permission or checklist-restart test.

features.title: Builder and templates
features.description: Rearrange the browser shell or start from a template, remove unused controls and hide apps or bars during focused work.
limitations: Builder/templates are listed in Free, but no layout, accessibility or recovery test was performed.
This concerns the current Shift Browser offering, not every legacy v9 workflow.

features.title: Per-Space app/tool stacks
features.description: Build separate app, tab and extension sets for projects or profiles, with account context switching that avoids repeatedly signing out.
limitations: Free lists five Spaces and ten apps per Space; Advanced lists unlimited Spaces/apps.
Documentation does not independently prove a complete isolation boundary or the behavior of external links.

features.title: App-integrated work
features.description: Keep app stacks and simultaneous inboxes available in a persistent sidebar, switching between accounts of the same service. The maker advertises a catalog exceeding 4,500 apps.
limitations: Catalog size and any-extension compatibility are vendor claims, not tested counts or universal support.
Free app-count limits apply; simultaneous inboxes do not establish every service's notification or identity behavior.

features.title: Explicit omnibox AI choice
features.description: An on-device intent router may suggest Ask AI, but the user selects the route: Tab starts AI while Enter continues to search or a URL. The launch article explains that automatic selection was rejected in favor of a hint.
limitations: The on-device component is described as an intent router, not proof of local-only AI inference.
No intent-classification, accidental-routing or keybinding test was run.

features.title: Visible, opt-in AI context
features.description: Selected text or page content appears as removable context chips in the AI input. The side panel can sit left or right, or expand into a dedicated conversation view while context remains user-controlled.
limitations: General AI usage is limited in Free and expanded in Advanced, without numeric quotas established here.
The specific opt-in explanation qualifies broad marketing about history-wide context; no data-flow or context-completeness test.

features.title: Independent AI controls
features.description: Disable AI Chat and Intelligent Omnibox independently from settings. The launch article distinguishes these shipped choices from future proactive suggestions and broader context improvements.
limitations: No persistence, re-enablement or enforcement test for either toggle.
Future proactive features mentioned by the author are not counted as shipped behavior.

features.title: Sidecar context with explicit tab mentions
features.description: Use the assistant alongside a page and add the current tab or tabs selected with @ mentions. The manual describes visible-text, headline and metadata extraction on each submitted request.
limitations: Extraction completeness, permission enforcement and request-level data flow were not tested.
Desktop panel documentation does not establish identical mobile UI or unlimited free concurrent work.

features.title: Reusable query Shortcuts
features.description: Create reusable prompts with sources, models and search modes, combine or share shortcuts, and invoke them through slash selection in search or the sidecar. Shortcut composition is separate from explicit submission.
limitations: The manual still labels an expanded shortcut library coming soon; library shipment is not assumed.
Sharing or selecting a prompt is not authority to perform its actions. No shortcut was executed.
Model/source availability and plan quotas were not audited.

features.title: Parallel Background Assistants
features.description: The October 2025 launch changelog assigns multiple simultaneous agentic tasks and one page for confirmations and follow-ups to Max subscribers.
limitations: Max entitlement is supported at the dated announcement, not by a current quota or billing inspection.
Android's guide explicitly limits automation to foreground use; desktop background behavior is not generalized to mobile.
No concurrency, cancellation or completion test.

features.title: Consumer and enterprise action controls
features.description: Consumer settings govern history/action access and site blocking. Enterprise admins can set Browser Control, Read Only or No Access by domain and control whether users may enable unconfirmed actions. Domain-specific rules are documented to override global assistant settings.
platforms: Documented Comet desktop and enterprise deployments; mobile policy parity unverified
limitations: Granular admin controls require Perplexity Enterprise and are not a consumer-wide entitlement claim.
An allow/read domain exception can remain effective despite global disablement according to documentation; this is not a locally reproduced bypass.
An unambiguous global stop and clear precedence are recommendation hypotheses, not established Chrome defects.

features.title: Two-tab split view
features.description: Open two tabs side by side through a tab/menu action, swap pane positions and separate them back into normal tabs. The manual also describes an Option-click shortcut.
platforms: Documented desktop UI; Windows/macOS shortcut parity unverified
limitations: No evidence for more than two panes or mobile split-view parity.
No focus, state-preservation or shortcut test was run.

features.title: Mobile continuity and action visibility
features.description: The iOS launch describes voice across open tabs and a conversation tied to page context across devices. Android documentation describes a visible AI-control border, step-by-step action review and automation only while the app remains open.
limitations: Features are platform-specific; the two mobile editions are not asserted to be identical.
Older no-mobile help text is superseded by explicit launches. iOS engine/minimum version remain unestablished.
No voice, synchronization, backgrounding or task-completion test.

features.title: In-page Ask ChatGPT
features.description: Historically, Ask ChatGPT supplied contextual assistance beside the current website, reducing the need to copy page material into a separate chat tab.
limitations: Atlas is retired; this is not currently supported functionality or a product recommendation.
No historical or current runtime behavior was tested.

features.title: Optional browser memories
features.description: The launch described optional browser memories that could be viewed or archived, with associated memories deleted through browsing-history deletion. The retirement article clarifies that Atlas browser memories are separate from ChatGPT memories and chat deletion does not remove Atlas-specific data.
limitations: Historical settings are not guaranteed accessible after retirement.
Deletion linkage and storage behavior are vendor statements, not a tested erasure guarantee.

features.title: Per-site page visibility
features.description: An address-bar control historically excluded selected sites from ChatGPT page visibility and browser-memory creation, independently of globally enabling memories.
limitations: Retired-browser control is historical design evidence only.
No per-site isolation, persistence or enforcement test was performed.

features.title: Agent mode in the browser
features.description: Agent mode launched in preview for Plus, Pro and Business with visible actions and pauses for certain sensitive sites. Business browser access was beta; Enterprise/Edu access required administrator enablement. Historical agent restrictions excluded browser code execution, downloads, extension installation and local filesystem or other-app access.
limitations: Both preview maturity and retirement apply; this is not a stable/current agent recommendation.
Launch-time plan entitlements and safeguards were not tested and do not guarantee error-free actions.
Windows, iOS and Android shipment was not established.

features.title: Ephemeral logged-out agent contexts
features.description: OWL's historical engineering account describes separate in-memory Chromium StoragePartitions for each logged-out agent session, discarded at completion instead of reusing the user's Incognito profile. It also describes routing agent input to web content rather than privileged browser shortcuts.
limitations: Maker architecture prose, not source-code inspection or an isolation/erasure test.
Atlas is retired and formerly preview-only behavior is not promoted to an active recommendation.

features.title: Tasks as context boundaries
features.description: Group related tabs, chats and requests into a self-contained Task. The shipping announcement describes an agent operating in that Task's context rather than accessing everything else in the browser.
limitations: Context isolation is a vendor claim, not tested enforcement.
Built-in agentic capabilities are subscription-limited; exact free Task-management scope was not established.
Initial sources describe Early Access; no stable graduation date was established, and this is not a deployment recommendation.

features.title: Neon Do control surface
features.description: Display planned steps and live page actions, with pause, stop, takeover and redirection controls. Neon Do interacts in the local browser session while relying on cloud models for plans and instructions.
limitations: Neon Do is a paid capability in the retained plan table; usage limits were not quantified.
Stop/takeover and sensitive-action confirmations were not tested; already committed external actions may require separate treatment.
Early Access history and residual prompt-injection risk prevent treating documentation as a stable safety guarantee.

features.title: Composable Cards/decks
features.description: Create, combine and save reusable instruction Cards, organized into decks, to specify output formats or recurring workflows across Chat, Do and Research Agents.
limitations: Skill Cards are listed in Standard; free-tier parity and library-wide quality were not established.
Imported/shared instructions do not authorize actions. No Card was executed or published.
Broader access is not proof of stable maturity for all agentic workflows.

features.title: Different research execution modes
features.description: The FAQ distinguishes Deep Research, One-Minute Research and Local Research. Local Research uses logged-in browser context and location/preferences-informed search results rather than solely a remote research environment.
limitations: Research is listed in Standard; specific quotas and model choices are volatile.
Local browser context does not establish local-only inference or zero server retention.
Research accuracy, task duration and stable maturity were not tested.

features.title: Background creation
features.description: The Make launch description uses a cloud virtual machine to continue creating while the user is offline and return editable source files and shareable output links. Current Standard also lists generation and scheduled-task capabilities.
limitations: Paid cloud capability, not offline local inference; no source/output export or scheduled-task test.
Task success, ownership of generated material and current quota limits were not independently verified.
Initial invitation/Early Access maturity is not silently upgraded to stable production readiness.

features.title: External-agent interface
features.description: Expose the live Neon browser through an MCP server or Browser CLI. The FAQ describes read-only default MCP access with explicit permission for clicks/form filling. Current Free lists the browser, MCP/CLI setup and basic Chat; the August announcement distinguishes account-required MCP from accountless browsing/CLI.
limitations: No external agent or personal browser session was connected; advertised defaults are not verified enforcement.
Older universal paid/account-required FAQ text conflicts with newer access evidence.
Free browser access does not make external models/services free or establish safe stable deployment of agentic actions.

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Treat these as Arc design precedents, not guarantees of Mac/Windows parity. The legacy command list also mentions Notes/Easels; those were deliberately not counted as current features. Arc’s old security page claims a 48-hour Chromium-update guarantee; the current download/farewell pages are stronger evidence for present lifecycle. Account dependence and approaching EOL make export/migration especially relevant. [R04-A2][R04-A3][R04-A4]

reportQualifications.label: V
reportQualifications.text: The farewell’s claim that Dia surpasses Arc in speed, stability, and security is not a benchmark from this lane. [R04-A1]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Do not carry its original Mac-only beta status forward. Conversely, do not declare every connector GA: Figma is marked GA on November 12; Ashby/Dropbox were marked beta October 29. Browsing is offered free and the Arc farewell calls AI optional, but paid AI entitlement details remain incomplete. [R04-D2][R04-A1][R04-D4]

reportQualifications.label: V
reportQualifications.text: E2E encryption describes Sync, not a proof that all AI processing stays on-device. The April 9 policy distinguishes account/content/Skills data and says content can be used to improve Dia unless the user opts out. Its policy also excludes under-18 use. [R04-D4]

reportQualifications.label: Source quote / boundary
reportQualifications.text: “Container Tabs separate your cookies/browsing sessions, but it doesn't separate your browsing history and extensions.” Workspace organization must not be marketed as complete profile isolation. [R04-Z4]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Source-only review; no claim that all historic window-sync limitations are fixed. Release notes explicitly describe initial Spaces-sync merging and earlier experimental window sync. The current release log also introduces Little Zen, but its placement among release blocks did not yield a reliable standalone ship date; it is not counted above. [R04-Z3]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Panel extension support and mobile user-agent behavior are not universal. Temporary feature freeze is a concrete maintenance-cost signal, not abandonment. Workspace tabs remaining open is not an independently verified guarantee against form-data loss. Floorp’s vendor-authored Chrome comparison table was not adopted as Chrome baseline evidence. [R04-F1][R04-F3][R04-F5]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Homepage currently lists free Basic with unlimited workspaces/limited Airis, Pro at $20/month and Max at $30/month. Older FAQ instead describes $10/month Pro and paid unlimited workspaces; do not reuse that older table as current pricing. Windows/iOS “coming soon” is not a shipped-platform finding. Chrome-extension support is described for popular extensions, not every extension. Account/backend availability and current security updates were not tested. [R04-S1][R04-S2]

reportQualifications.label: V
reportQualifications.text: Battery, performance, AI quality, and “first” claims are vendor assertions. [R04-S1][R04-S6]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: These are historical inspiration, not supported current functionality. AppSumo still retains “lifetime” purchase copy beneath the sunset notice; that is not evidence of a live offer. The Microsoft Store retrieval produced only a listing title, not usable current download/support proof. This lane does not promote unverified historic Chromium/Mac/Linux details into maker-confirmed facts. No evidence here establishes that Comet preserves Sidekick Sessions or app isolation. [R04-K1][R04-K2][R04-K3]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: App integrations are enhanced web tabs, not necessarily native app capabilities. The many organization layers add conceptual overhead (H). Team deployment, Sync, and AI have distinct subscription/data boundaries. “Always up-to-date,” productivity gains, and certification-in-progress language are vendor claims, not audits or current certifications established here. AI can be disabled according to the homepage. [R04-W1][R04-W2]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Free currently lists five Spaces, ten apps per Space, Builder/templates, and limited AI. Advanced is shown as $199.99 USD annually with unlimited Spaces/apps and expanded AI. Those are observed page terms, not a quote guaranteed beyond retrieval. Broad marketing about cross-history context should not override the more specific opt-in explanation. “Strictly private” is a vendor claim; the on-device router does not prove all AI inference is on-device. [R04-H6][R04-H4][R04-H5]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Current mobile launch evidence supersedes stale “no mobile” help pages. Android docs specify Android 12+ and no background work. Desktop docs exclude Linux/ChromeOS; iOS engine/parity remains unverified. Most Chrome extensions are supported except extensions replacing the new-tab page. [R04-C1][R04-C2][R04-C8][R04-C11]

reportQualifications.label: Important documented policy detail
reportQualifications.text: Enterprise domain rules can override global assistant settings, including making a domain readable/actionable despite globally disabled assistant access. This is an explicit documentation statement, not a tested bypass. A proposed Chrome control should make precedence obvious and offer an unambiguous global stop. [R04-C6]

reportQualifications.label: V
reportQualifications.text: Local default storage and “minimal context” transfer are privacy claims; the docs also acknowledge sending context to Perplexity to fulfill requests. Marketing demonstrations are not reliable task-completion measurements. [R04-C4][R04-C13]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Windows/iOS/Android were “coming soon” at launch; no shipment was verified here. The original agent mode was restricted from installing extensions, downloading files, running browser code, or accessing the local filesystem. Retired Atlas tabs/history do not automatically transfer, and recovery is not guaranteed. Exact final shutdown date remains unverified in the readable maker retirement article. [R04-T1][R04-T2]

reportQualifications.label: V
reportQualifications.text: OWL’s startup/responsiveness and isolation benefits are engineering claims, not measured results from this lane. The architecture account says agent input is delivered to web content rather than privileged browser shortcuts. [R04-T3]

reportQualifications.label: Restrictions/tradeoffs
reportQualifications.text: Windows/Mac only verified; mobile is future work. Older FAQ says paid/account-required universally, whereas the newer free-access article distinguishes accountless browsing/CLI from account-required MCP. Current plan page is stronger for tier availability. Model lists are volatile and are not reproduced as a current compatibility promise. [R04-N2][R04-N3][R04-N5]

reportQualifications.label: V / data boundary
reportQualifications.text: Neon Do interacts locally but uses cloud LLMs. FAQ states server retention of 365 days for chats/workflows and provides deletion controls; “local” is not a zero-retention claim. Security article explicitly admits residual prompt-injection risk and describes confirmations, blocked high-risk pages, and proposed future defenses separately. [R04-N2][R04-N6]
